Align.description:
Put every stream on one regular time grid.

Each grid point takes the stream's sample at exactly that time if there is
one, even if that sample is missing. (Rows flagged ``NO_SAMPLE``, which a join
of several inputs adds, aren't samples.) Otherwise it takes a value from nearby
valid samples, chosen by ``method``, and is flagged ``RESAMPLED``. With no
valid sample within ``tolerance``, the point is NaN and flagged ``MISSING``.
The grid is anchored at multiples of ``freq`` from the Unix epoch, so the
same data always gives the same grid.

how.description: outer: the grid spans every stream's data; inner: only the time all streams cover.
how.title: How

method.description: nearest: the closest valid sample; previous: the last valid sample at or before the grid time; linear: time-weighted between the valid samples either side.
method.title: Method

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

tolerance.description: nearest/previous: how far away a sample may be (default: freq). linear: the largest allowed gap between the two samples either side (default: 2 x freq).
tolerance.title: Tolerance

Align.title: Align

Calibrate.description:
Correct a stream against an intermittent, trusted reference.

1. **Fit.** On the *trusted rows*, the rows where the reference has a value
   and ``fit_when`` holds, fit a model that maps the ``features`` (by default
   the target itself) to the reference.
2. **Apply.** Predict the corrected value wherever ``apply_when`` holds and
   the features have values. These values are flagged ``CORRECTED``, on top
   of the target's own flags. Where ``apply_when`` is false, the target's
   value passes through unchanged.
3. **Prefer the reference.** With ``prefer_reference``, the trusted rows take
   the reference's own value and flags instead of a prediction.
4. **Follow drift.** With ``refit={"rolling": "1D"}``, the model is refitted
   for each block of time on the trusted rows of the window ending with that
   block. The model fitted on the training data covers blocks whose window
   has too few trusted rows.

The fitted state holds the coefficients (or the formula's parameters) and fit
metrics: rows used, RMSE and R².

Models (``model``): the linear models of
:data:`~flexsignal.backends.models.LINEAR_MODELS`, e.g.
``sklearn:HuberRegressor``, or ``scipy:curve_fit`` with a ``formula`` such as
``"a + b * A + c * A ** 2"`` and ``initial`` values for its parameters.

With ``mode="residual"`` the model predicts the error, ``reference - target``,
and the corrected value is ``target + prediction``. Use it when the features
explain the error rather than the value, e.g. a temperature that biases A.

apply_when.description: Where to correct the target (default: everywhere). Elsewhere the target's value passes through unchanged.
apply_when.title: Apply When

features.description: Model inputs (default: the target). Not used with scipy:curve_fit, whose formula names its inputs.
features.title: Features

fit_when.description: When the reference can be trusted, e.g. 'C == 0 and D == 0 and B > 0'. Default: wherever it has a value.
fit_when.title: Fit When

formula.description: For scipy:curve_fit: the model as a formula of streams and parameters, e.g. 'a + b * A'.
formula.title: Formula

initial.description: For scipy:curve_fit: a starting value for each parameter in the formula, e.g. {a: 0, b: 1}.
initial.title: Initial

mode.description: map: predict the reference value; residual: predict reference - target and add it to the target.
mode.title: Mode

model.description: The model: a linear model key such as sklearn:HuberRegressor or statsmodels:RLM, or scipy:curve_fit with a formula.
model.title: Model

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

output.description: Name of the corrected stream (default: <target>_clean). Set it to the target's name to replace the target.
output.title: Output

params.description: Keyword arguments for the model, e.g. {alpha: 1.0} for Ridge.
params.title: Params

prefer_reference.description: Use the reference's own value on the rows where it is trusted.
prefer_reference.title: Prefer Reference

reference.description: The trusted stream measuring the same quantity, e.g. B.
reference.title: Reference

refit.description: static: one model fitted on the training data; or {rolling: 1D} to refit on a moving window and follow drift.
refit.title: Refit

target.description: The stream to correct, e.g. A.
target.title: Target

units.description: Units of the output (default: the target's units).
units.title: Units

Detotalize.description:
Turn a running total (a totalizer or counter) into a rate.

Each valid sample gets the increase since the previous valid sample, divided
by the time between them, per ``per``: a total in m^3 with ``per="1h"`` gives
m^3/hr. The rate is stamped at the end of its interval, and carries the flags
of both samples. The first valid sample has no rate and is flagged
``MISSING``.

A counter that wraps around at ``rollover`` (e.g. 999999) is unwrapped. A
total that drops with no ``rollover`` set was reset; the rate across the
reset is unknown, so it is left missing and flagged ``OUT_OF_RANGE``.

name.title: Name

per.description: Time unit of the rate, e.g. 1h.
per.title: Per

rollover.description: Value at which the counter wraps back to 0.
rollover.title: Rollover

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

units.description: Units of the rate, e.g. m^3/hr (default: unchanged).
units.title: Units

Detotalize.title: Detotalize

Filter.description:
Smooth noise out of a stream.

- ``savgol``: a Savitzky-Golay filter (:func:`scipy.signal.savgol_filter`)
  fits a polynomial of degree ``polyorder`` across a moving ``window``. It
  keeps peaks better than a moving average.
- ``butterworth``: a low-pass Butterworth filter of ``order``, run forwards
  and backwards so it adds no delay (:func:`scipy.signal.sosfiltfilt`). It
  removes variation faster than ``cutoff``, a period such as 30min.
- ``median``: a centred moving median over ``window``. It removes spikes as
  well as noise, but flattens sharp peaks.

Every smoothed value is flagged ``FILTERED``. Missing values stay missing.
``savgol`` and ``butterworth`` need a regular index and filter each unbroken
run of values separately; a run too short for the filter is left as it is.

cutoff.description: butterworth: the shortest period of variation to keep, e.g. 1h.
cutoff.title: Cutoff

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

polyorder.description: savgol: degree of the fitted polynomial.
polyorder.title: Polyorder

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

window.description: savgol and median: width of the moving window, e.g. 30min.
window.title: Window

Hampel.description:
Reject spikes with a Hampel filter: a rolling median plus a robust spread.

Each value is compared with the median of a centred time window. It is
flagged ``OUTLIER`` if it lies more than ``n_sigma`` robust standard deviations
from that median. The robust standard deviation is
1.4826 × the window's median absolute deviation; 1.4826 is the fixed factor
that makes this match the standard deviation for normal data, so ``n_sigma``
is the only threshold to tune. See Pearson, R. K. (2002),
"Outliers in process modeling and identification", IEEE Trans. Control
Systems Technology 10(1), 55-63, doi:10.1109/87.974338.

The window should be several times wider than the spikes being removed, and
narrow enough that the signal's own trend changes little across it.

A spread estimated from a short window can come out much smaller than the
real noise, and then ordinary noise gets flagged. This happens most where
the signal is flat. Set ``min_scale`` to the sensor's noise standard
deviation, or its resolution, to put a floor under the spread.

min_periods.description: Fewest valid samples a window needs before it can flag.
min_periods.title: Min Periods

min_scale.description: Floor on the robust standard deviation, in the stream's units; typically the sensor's noise level.
min_scale.title: Min Scale

n_sigma.description: How many robust standard deviations count as an outlier.
n_sigma.title: N Sigma

name.description: Optional label for this step, shown in provenance and reports. Must be unique within a spec.
name.title: Name

streams.description: The streams this step acts on.
streams.title: Streams

window.description: Width of the centred window, e.g. 1h.
window.title: Window

Hampel.title: Hampel

Interpolate.description:
Fill short interior gaps by interpolating between the valid values either side.

Only gaps no longer than ``max_gap`` are filled: on 5-minute data,
``max_gap="15min"`` fills up to two missing samples in a row. Gaps at the
start or end of the data are never filled. Filled values gain
``IMPUTED_SHORT``.

Methods use numpy and scipy:

- ``linear``: :func:`numpy.interp`;
- ``nearest`` and ``previous``: :class:`scipy.interpolate.interp1d`;
- ``pchip``: :class:`scipy.interpolate.PchipInterpolator`, shape-preserving
  with no overshoot;
- ``akima``: :class:`scipy.interpolate.Akima1DInterpolator`.

Iterative.description:
Fill each stream from a model of the others, round-robin (MICE-style).

Uses :class:`sklearn.impute.IterativeImputer` with its default Bayesian
ridge model, on the ``streams`` and ``features`` scaled to unit variance. It
learns from the data it fills, so ``fit`` stores nothing; the random state is
fixed, so results are repeatable. Filled values gain ``IMPUTED_MODEL``.

Fill a value from the rows whose other streams are most similar.

Uses :class:`sklearn.impute.KNNImputer` on the ``streams`` and ``features``,
each scaled to unit variance first so units don't decide the distance. It
learns from the data it fills, so ``fit`` stores nothing. Filled values gain

Kalman.description:
Fill gaps with the Kalman smoother of a structural time-series model.

Each stream is modelled as a level (``local_level``), or a level with a slope
(``local_linear_trend``), plus optional ``seasonal`` cycles and noise, using
:class:`statsmodels.tsa.statespace.structural.UnobservedComponents`. ``fit``
estimates the model's variances on the training data by maximum likelihood
and stores them as JSON. ``transform`` runs the Kalman smoother with those
values, which estimates every missing value from the data on both sides of
it. Filled values gain ``IMPUTED_MODEL``.

It needs a regular time index; run ``align`` or ``resample`` first. A long
gap relaxes towards the level and cycles, so set ``seasonal`` when the
stream has a daily pattern.

RateOfChange.description:
Reject values that change faster than the process physically can.

Each value is compared with the last *accepted* value. If
``|change| / elapsed time`` exceeds ``max_rate`` per ``per``, the value is
flagged ``RATE_OF_CHANGE``. A spike is caught without flagging the point
after it, because that point is compared with the last good value before the
spike. A genuine step change is accepted once enough time has passed for the
allowed rate to cover it.

Structural.description:
Forecast with a structural time-series model (statsmodels' UnobservedComponents).

The target is modelled as a level (``local_level``) or a level with a slope
(``local_linear_trend``), plus ``seasonal`` cycles, an optional
``autoregressive`` term for slowly decaying departures, a linear effect of
each ``exog`` stream, and noise. ``fit`` estimates the model's parameters by
maximum likelihood on the training data and stores them as JSON;
``transform`` runs the Kalman filter over the new data's history with those
parameters and forecasts from the issue time. The intervals come from the
model's forecast variance. Missing target values in the history are fine;
``exog`` streams need a value at every time step.

Tiered.description:
Route each gap to an imputer by its length.

Short gaps are best interpolated; long ones need a model. For example::

    tiers=[
        {"max_gap": "15min", "method": "interpolate"},
        {"max_gap": "6h", "method": "regression",
         "options": {"features": ["pressure"]}},
        {"max_gap": None, "method": "kalman"},
    ]

A gap goes to the first tier whose ``max_gap`` covers its length, measured in
the data as it arrives at this step. Each tier's imputer is fitted on the
training data, and its state is kept under ``tiers``. Filled values carry the
flag of the method that filled them.

Tukey.description:
Reject values beyond Tukey's fences, learned from the training data.

``fit`` records each stream's quartiles Q1 and Q3. Values below
``Q1 - k·IQR`` or above ``Q3 + k·IQR`` are flagged ``OUTLIER``, where
IQR = Q3 - Q1. Use k = 1.5 for "outliers" and k = 3 for "far out" values
(Tukey, J. W. (1977), *Exploratory Data Analysis*, Addison-Wesley).

This suits streams whose normal range doesn't drift. For a signal with a
strong trend or regimes, prefer ``hampel``.

flexsignal__steps__forecast__Regression.description:
Forecast with a linear model of cycles, exog streams and lagged values.

The inputs at each time are:

- sine and cosine terms for each ``fourier`` cycle;
- each ``exog`` stream at that time (known ahead);
- the target itself ``lags`` earlier: the forecast is then made one step at a
  time, each step using the ones before it;
- each ``past`` stream ``past_lags`` earlier. Those streams are known only up to
  the issue time, so every ``past_lags`` must be at least the horizon.

``fit`` learns one model per target on the training rows where the target and
all its inputs have values, and stores the coefficients as JSON. The
intervals are the training residuals' quantiles; they don't widen with lead
time, so with ``lags`` they understate the uncertainty far ahead.

issue_time.title: Issue Time

lags.description: Also use the target this long before, e.g. [1h, 1D].
lags.title: Lags

model.description: A linear model key: least squares by default, or e.g. sklearn:Ridge with params {alpha: ...} when there are many inputs.

flexsignal__steps__impute__Regression.description:
Fill gaps from a linear model of other streams and of time of day or week.

The inputs are the ``features`` streams, each also at every lag in ``lags``,
and sine and cosine terms for each ``fourier`` cycle. ``fit`` learns one model
per stream on the training rows where the stream and all its inputs have
values, and stores the coefficients as JSON. ``transform`` fills a gap
wherever the inputs have values. Filled values gain ``IMPUTED_MODEL``.

Models are the linear models of
:data:`~flexsignal.backends.models.LINEAR_MODELS`, e.g. ``sklearn:Ridge``.
